newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says lower Italy inflation now structural.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says lower Italy inflation now structural.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said falling inflation in Italy was now part of a "structural and permanent" process that would continue in coming months.

In a speech opening the annual Fiera del Levante trade fair in Bari, southern Italy, he said successive monthly falls in consumer price inflation reflected changing patterns of behaviour and more realistic exchange rate levels.
Year-on-year consumer price inflation fell to 3.4 percent in August from 3.6 percent in July.
"The fall to 3.4 percent in August is neither casual nor episodic," Prodi said.
"The disinflationary (tendencies) which derive from a change in behaviour among Italians and more realistic exchange rate levels should strengthen in the coming months."
He said an agreement between government and trades unions in July 1993 to end a system of inflation-linked wage indexation was at the root of what he called "this structural adjustment".

"Domestic and international economic operators now concur in the view that, apart from in the case of extraordinary and unpredictable events, the process of falling living costs is permanent and structural," Prodi said.
